minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted a $50 fine against a resident for repeated unleashed dogs at McNiff Park despite an ADA claim
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission approved a beach-use request from a community club, set capital plan priorities (Fitzgerald Field regrading topping the list, Northfield Park kept on the list), and uncovered a $30,000 error in the Marshall Park project's remaining budget that it referred to the town accountant and manager. After lengthy public comment from baseball program members, it voted to issue a $50 fine to one of two residents for repeatedly bringing unleashed dogs onto McNiff Park's ball field despite their claim the dogs were ADA service animals. The commission also reviewed master plan committee feedback, got an update on hiring a new recreation director, and set upcoming meeting dates.

what_happened.line: The commission voted a fine against a resident for repeated unleashed-dog violations at McNiff Park despite a claimed ADA exemption.
The commission voted to make Fitzgerald Field regrading the top capital-plan priority, ahead of Northfield Park and other projects.
A discrepancy was found in the Marshall Park project's remaining budget and referred to the town accountant and manager.
The commission approved a community club's request to use the town beach for its annual fundraiser.

why_it_matters: The dog-fine vote tests how the town enforces park rules against a claimed ADA exemption, using a schedule that escalates on repeat offenses, while no dedicated park enforcement officer has yet been assigned.
The capital-plan ranking decides which park project the town funds first, directly affecting the ball field youth leagues use for games.
The Marshall Park budget discrepancy touches a federal ARPA grant with a year-end spending deadline, so how it is resolved could affect whether that funding is used or lost.
